approachQuestion.prompt:
Two Separate Recording Slots

Array `quality` contains signed scores for consecutive minutes. Choose two non-overlapping contiguous recording slots, one of length a and one of length b, to maximize their combined sum. Either slot may occur first; slots may touch. Return only the greatest combined sum.

Limits and assumptions:
• 2 ≤ n ≤ 200000; a ≥ 1; b ≥ 1; a+b ≤ n; -10^6 ≤ quality[i] ≤ 10^6.
• Do not modify quality. All sums fit in signed 64-bit integers. Both slots must be selected, even for all-negative input.

Examples:
1. quality = [5,-10,4,3,2], a = 1, b = 2 → 12, using [5] and [4,3].
2. quality = [-5,-2,-3], a = 1, b = 1 → -5.

Choose one approach.
constraints: Do not modify quality. All sums fit in signed 64-bit integers. Both slots must be selected, even for all-negative input.

options.text: First assume the a-slot precedes the b-slot. As the b-slot moves right, maintain its sum and the greatest sum among all a-slots ending before it starts, adding one newly eligible a-slot per move. Repeat with a and b exchanged and take the greater answer.
options.feedback: For each later slot, all earlier non-overlapping slots are summarized by their best sum. Both sweeps cover both possible orders.

options.text: Build prefix sums and arrays of the best earlier length-a and length-b slot sums. Evaluate every later slot against the corresponding best disjoint earlier slot.
options.feedback: This covers all disjoint pairs correctly but stores summaries that can be maintained in scalar state during two sweeps.

options.text: Choose the individually greatest length-a and length-b slots and add their sums, allowing them to overlap.
options.feedback: For quality [10,9,0], a=b=1 this can select index zero twice for twenty, but the best legal total is nineteen.

options.text: Perform only the sweep where the a-slot occurs before the b-slot.
options.feedback: For quality [5,5,-100,9], a=1,b=2 the best has the b-slot first, yielding nineteen; forcing a first gives at most minus eighty-six.

feedback.reason: For each later slot, bestEarlier includes only earlier slots ending before it starts.
details: For order (p,q), initialize the p-slot [0,p-1] and q-slot [p,p+q-1], and initialize bestEarlier from that real p-slot. For each next q start s, update the rolling p-slot ending at s-1 and bestEarlier, update the q-slot sum, and combine them. Run (a,b) and (b,a), retaining no arrays or slices.

For each later slot, bestEarlier includes only earlier slots ending before it starts. Both length orders are necessary because the a-slot may occur before or after the b-slot. Initialize from actual slots to preserve negative optima.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Sweep each order with rolling sums” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two sequential ordered sweeps reuse rolling sums and scalar maxima.
details: For any fixed later slot, bestEarlier summarizes exactly all disjoint earlier slots of the prescribed length. Both orders exhaust legal solutions. Each sweep initializes and moves two fixed-length sums in linear work, with scalar state. Initializing from real slots handles negative inputs.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Each length order uses two rolling sums and one prefix maximum; it does not enumerate every pair of disjoint slots.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: No sorting, cumulative-sum arrays, or saved slot list is used; both sweeps retain only scalar summaries.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: bestEarlier replaces a list of earlier slot sums, so memory does not grow with the number of starts.
